output.name: Sekra
output.myth: Sekra was the first gull to follow Aun up the cut string, because she wanted to see where the wind went too. She flew so high that frost stiffened her wings, and Tavo the Gale came down laughing and took hold of her tail. He pulled three feathers out for the joke, then let her go. She fell into the cold sea and was too heavy to climb back. Hilun, the Windward Gull, watched from the north and did not laugh. Hesk counted the feathers from the pole and tallied them. Sekra came home low over the cliffs, past the Shag with Wings Out on her wet rock, who had her wings held out to dry and said nothing for once. She teaches the young ones to hang on the wind rather than climb it. The Gulls still call her name at dusk. The old women say it is a message: the string is still tied at the north end, if anyone thinks to pull. Mend your net while you wait, as Ennu mended the gull in the surf. Tavo does not care who waits.
output.finding: Start from the Mended Gull, Nalsa, which sits a fist to the north-west of Sekra, and go one fist south-east to find her.
